# Happy Path Programming: full episode notes

> No-frills discussions between Bruce Eckel and James Ward about programming, what it is, and what it should be.

Every episode of the Happy Path Programming podcast by Bruce Eckel and James Ward, newest first. The index is [llms.txt](https://happypathprogramming.com/llms.txt).

## #123 Beyond 4GL with Leo Gorodinski

- Page: https://happypathprogramming.com/episodes/123-beyond-4gl-with-leo-gorodinski.html
- Aired: November 20, 2026 · 1h 09m · with Leo Gorodinski
- Topics: AI & LLMs, Language Design, Types, Architecture & Design, Databases & Data
- Listen: [Play on Spotify](https://podcasters.spotify.com/pod/show/happypathprogramming/episodes/123-Beyond-4GL-with-Leo-Gorodinski-e3somte), [Play on Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/123-beyond-4gl-with-leo-gorodinski/id1531666706?i=1000803213144)

James and Bruce talk with Leo Gorodinski, formerly of Jet.com and Alvys, about Cohesive, a language he's building for describing whole SaaS systems instead of individual computations. Leo argues that English won't replace code, and that the real bottleneck in agentic coding is trust: you have to be able to verify that what the AI built matches what you meant. Cohesive works at a higher level than general-purpose languages. You define entities, relationships, processes, APIs and infrastructure bindings, and Cohesive compiles them down to C# and TypeScript. They discuss why Leo chose term-level invariants over ever more powerful type systems, how categorical systems theory, CRDTs and the CALM theorem shaped the design, what SQL and 4GLs got right, escape hatches and the capability cliff, and Leo's benchmarks comparing agents building with Cohesive against agents using conventional stacks.

Resources:

- [Leo Gorodinski](https://x.com/eulerfx)
- [Cohesive website](https://cohesive.sh)
- [Cohesive Systems on GitHub](https://github.com/cohesivesystems)
- [Cohesive .NET libraries](https://github.com/cohesivesystems/cohesive)
- [Cohesive evals (the benchmarks)](https://github.com/cohesivesystems/cohesive-evals)
- [Knowledge graph](https://github.com/cohesivesystems/knowledge)
- [Catalogue of agent languages](https://github.com/cohesivesystems/agentlanguages)
- [Leo's writing on Medium](https://medium.com/@eulerfx)
- [Dijkstra, "On the foolishness of 'natural language programming'" (EWD667)](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~EWD/transcriptions/EWD06xx/EWD667.html)
- [Niu & Spivak, Polynomial Functors: A Mathematical Theory of Interaction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.00990)
- [Hellerstein & Alvaro, "Keeping CALM: When Distributed Consistency Is Easy"](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.01930)
- [Jepsen (Kyle Kingsbury's database testing)](https://jepsen.io)
- [Effect (TypeScript)](https://effect.website)
- [ZIO (Scala)](https://zio.dev)
- [Lean](https://lean-lang.org)
- [Idris 2](https://www.idris-lang.org)
- [Granule](https://granule-project.github.io)
- [Winter Tech Forum](https://www.wintertechforum.com)

## #120 Aver AI-Native Programming Language with Szymon Teżewski

- Page: https://happypathprogramming.com/episodes/120-aver-ai-native-programming-language-with-szymon-tezewski.html
- Aired: June 02, 2026 · 1h 10m · with Szymon Teżewski
- Topics: Effect Oriented, AI & LLMs, Types, Testing, Language Design
- Listen: [Play on Spotify](https://podcasters.spotify.com/pod/show/happypathprogramming/episodes/120-Aver-AI-Native-Programming-Language-with-Szymon-Teewski-e3k8i8o), [Play on Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/120-aver-ai-native-programming-language-with-szymon/id1531666706?i=1000770840671), [Watch on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D_mPxGtSzbQ), [Discuss on Discord](https://discord.gg/XVKD2uPKyF)

We dive into the new Aver programming language with its creator, Szymon Teżewski: The AI-native language where code explains itself.

Aver is a language where every function carries its intent, side effects are visible in the type system, and tests are executable specs next to the code. The optimization target is the reviewer, not the generator.

Resources:

- [Aver](https://averlang.dev/)
- [Agent Languages](https://agentlanguages.dev/)

## #116 Infrastructure as Effects with Sam Goodwin

- Page: https://happypathprogramming.com/episodes/116-infrastructure-as-effects-with-sam-goodwin.html
- Aired: September 19, 2025 · 58m 57s · with Sam Goodwin
- Topics: Effect Oriented, Cloud & Serverless
- Listen: [Play on Spotify](https://podcasters.spotify.com/pod/show/happypathprogramming/episodes/116-Infrastructure-as-Effects-with-Sam-Goodwin-e38fbg3), [Play on Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/116-infrastructure-as-effects-with-sam-goodwin/id1531666706?i=1000727576032), [Watch on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YEn4A7XxgF4), [Discuss on Discord](https://discord.gg/XVKD2uPKyF)

Infrastructure as Code (IaC) is "code" but without most of the benefits of being code. Sam Goodwin is reinventing IaC with Alchemy and an upcoming Alchemy Effect project which aims to manage infrastructure dependencies & provisioning in the same way we manage requirements in Effect Oriented Programming.

Resources:

- [Sam Goodwin](https://x.com/samgoodwin89)
- [Alchemy](https://alchemy.run)
